issues.description: RevokeErr exposed via API without sanitization or capability gating despite author flagging it as a security concern
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this as the central issue. The PR author themselves asks whether displaying revoke_error is safe; backend error strings routinely leak DB driver messages, URLs, paths, and credential fragments. Either redact/truncate, gate behind a sudo/root capability, or document a backend invariant that revoke errors contain no sensitive content. The precondition must be stated and enforced before merge.

issues.description: FetchLeaseTimes renamed to FetchLeaseInfo breaks exported API with no compatibility shim
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager; renaming forces every out-of-tree caller to change for cosmetic reasons. Either keep the old name as a thin deprecated wrapper/alias or revert the rename. The broader postcondition can be documented without churning the symbol.

issues.description: Metric label fetch-lease-times left stale after function rename
issues.detail: metrics.MeasureSince still emits the literal 'fetch-lease-times' key while the function is now FetchLeaseInfo. Either keep the metric name with a comment explaining the intentional stability, or rename it as a deliberate telemetry change. Silent mismatches between code and metrics confuse operators later.

issues.description: Test coverage only asserts path; namespace_path and revoke_error branches are unexercised
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases checks resp.Data['path'] but never exercises namespace_path (lease in child namespace) or revoke_error (forced revoke failure) — the two fields with security-relevant content. There are also no assertions that sensitive members like InternalData, ClientToken, or Auth are absent from the response. Three small assertions would cover the actual surface this PR adds.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport is a hand-rolled projection with no structural redaction invariant
issues.detail: The function enumerates fields from leaseEntry with no typed projection or test that fails when leaseEntry grows. When a future sensitive field is added to leaseEntry, nothing forces a decision about whether it leaks. Define an explicit ExportedLeaseInfo struct so the shape is the contract, or add an assertion test that pins the export surface.

issues.description: Drive-by context substitution in one test is inconsistent with surrounding tests
issues.detail: namespace.RootContext(nil) was swapped for namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) at line 2450 while parallel tests in the same file kept nil. Either change is fine, but doing one and not the others buries unrelated churn in a rename commit. Pick one shape consistently or split the change out with its own justification.

synthesis.summary: All three reviewers converge on the same central concern the author already raised: revoke_error is backend-supplied text shipped to clients on a non-privileged endpoint with no sanitization or capability gate, and that boundary must be decided before merge. The FetchLeaseTimes rename is gratuitous churn on an exported API and leaves the metric label stale. Tests cover only one of three new fields and never assert absence of sensitive members. The shape of the change is small and reasonable; gate or sanitize revoke_error, revert or alias the rename, fix the metric, and expand test coverage to the actual new surface.
